about: Readings that rest on press reports and still need checking at the primary source. Work through at most two per morning; remove an item once done.

items.task: Calls B (North America Water) and F (Europe Land) were added on 23 Nov 2026 with baseline readings not checked at a primary source. Checked on 25 Nov 2026 and updated: B4, B6, B5, B7, F1, F2, F5, F6, F7, F8. Still to do: B1 (confirm at California's legislature site whether the water-supply assessment duty under Assembly Bill 2469 starts on 1 Jan 2028, not 2027; check the Virginia, New Jersey, Utah, Marana and Chandler rules); B3 (no source found for Georgia utilities refusing large water requests: find one or soften the reading); F3 (the Alixan court order of 10 Jul 2026 was read and gives long-term power above 60 megawatts, not 40; the 63 and 26 site figures are press-only and the 26 dates from January 2026; check Légifrance for any decree granting the status); F4 (the European Data Centre Monitor's own page and publisher were not found; the count is second-hand); F5 (Dutch, Amsterdam and Frankfurt rules at source). (Letters as relettered on 25 Nov 2026.)

Nineteen signposts were added on 23 Nov 2026 (seventeen remain: the owner dropped the old A8 and A11 on 25 Nov 2026 and A9 and A10 became A8 and A9) with readings from search results and press. Checked on 25 Nov 2026 and updated: A7, A8, A9, C5, C6, D4, D5, E6, E7, F8, G6, G7. Still to do: H3 (outcome of Thailand's board meeting of 27 Nov 2026; no official draft found, and the 80% figure and the date rest on one press chain); H4 (press shows the reclaimed-water agreements were signed on 11 Aug 2025 between the national sewerage company and Johor Special Water, not in June 2026 with the state water company, and the 'about 8.5 gigawatts' figure could not be found for Johor: correct once a primary source is read); H5 (the water regulator's dam status page would not open); H6 (Karnataka and Rajasthan policy documents not found; Rajasthan's wastewater requirement unconfirmed); C4 (the owner must choose one tracker; counts today range from 40 to over 1,000 depending on the tracker, and the 76 and 54 figures date from August and July 2026); A7 (open the regulator's orders for the second and third lines); G6 (find a company document confirming the third Inzai transformer entered service). Trigger wording on all seventeen is a draft awaiting the owner's confirmation; do not change a status on them until he confirms it.

Done on 25 Nov 2026: G2 reading updated from Osaka's paper of 9 Oct 2026; the owner kept Not yet. Still to read: the meeting minutes (1009gizi.pdf) and the grid operator's capacity map behind the '3 to 5 years where spare' figure.

A3 each quarter: add Mitsubishi Heavy Industries' large-frame orders and shipments (and its US units) beside GE Vernova's, and Doosan Enerbility's US orders from its announcements. Find a primary statement of the earliest delivery year on sale (results deck or call transcript) for GE Vernova and Mitsubishi. Confirm the first-half 2026 US order count by maker at a better source than the press report. Large frames for utilities only.

Find an original source (the Johor state government or Bernama) for the reported request that operators hold water-cooled expansions until mid-2027. The air-cooling statement of 10 Mar 2026 is already confirmed at Bernama and the owner kept the status at Not yet on 20 Nov 2026. Checked on 21 Nov 2026: no original source found. The mid-2027 hold traces to a South China Morning Post report citing unnamed officials (repeated by Lowyat, 20 Nov 2025). A Bernama report of a written parliamentary reply by the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (11 Feb 2026, carried by EdgeProp) says that as of January 2026 no data centre investment had been deferred. Still to try: a Johor state statement from around November 2025, and The Edge Malaysia's report (https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/781121).

Checked on 25 Nov 2026 in the grid operator's Senate presentation of 29 Jul 2026 and monthly overviews: queue about 474 gigawatts; 8,926 megawatts approved to energise in June 2026 and 9,456 in July; observed peak consumption 3,966 megawatts in June and 4,370 in July. The split '3.2 gigawatts approved plus 5.9 energised' on the A2 chart could not be confirmed and the figures read point elsewhere; the chart lines came from the owner's figures, so ask him before changing them.

Confirm at the federal regulator that Southwest Power Pool filed its large-load response on 20 Nov 2026 (press says it did; reported dockets ER27-559, ER27-577, ER27-578), and whether the regulator's errata of 18 Nov moved the comment dates for New York's grid operator (to 14 Dec) and PJM's transmission owners (to 15 Jan 2027), as a third-party tracker says.

Done on 25 Nov 2026: 14,609 megawatts applied with the owner's approval. Still to do: check the restart date of Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Unit 6 (the reading's source says 9 Feb 2026; a press headline says 21 Jan 2026), and check the earlier chart points against the Japan Atomic Industrial Forum's sheets (tell the owner before changing any).

The 'over 50%' share on the C1 card was not found on the tracker's second-quarter 2026 page (which confirms 45 projects and nearly US$68 billion). Find where the share comes from or ask the owner. The third-quarter 2026 report was not yet published on 25 Nov 2026.

H1's 'track' text and H4's reading mention about 8.5 gigawatts on the way in Johor; the nearest figure found (a parliamentary reply reported on 20 Oct 2026) is 8.39 gigawatts of peak data centre demand for Peninsular Malaysia by 2030, of which Johor 4.42. Check and correct with the owner.
